To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
single hurdle application of a sanitizer in a simulated dump or double hurdle application in the packing shed was not sufficient to reduce L. monocytogens on cantaloupes.

application of 5% Levulinic acid and Sodium Dodecyl sulfate in packing shed wash tanks significantly reduced L. monocyogenes at the cantaloupe stem scar compared to application of 200 ppm chlorine in simulated dump and dip treatments.
single hurdle applications of 5% LA/2% SDS in either a simulated dip or dump treatment reduced L. monocycygenes at the stem scar but did not reduce populations on the rind.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of single and double hurdle sanitizer applications in simulated field and packing shed operations for cantaloupes contaminated with Listeria.
developing and evaluating packing shed sanitation procedures that will effectively reduce L. monocytogens on cantaloupe rinds and stems.
the development of a double hurdle approach that would provide greater pathogen reduction than a single hurdle approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
single or double hurdle sanitizer applications in packing sheds or simulated packing sheds are not sufficient to reduce L. monocytogens to safe levels in cantaloupes.
the application of sanitizers to melons in the field is more effective than applying the same sanitizers only in the packing plant.
a double hurdle approach in a simulated dump application was less effective at reducing stem scar populations than a single hurdle approach in either simulated dump or dip treatments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single application of the sanitizer 5% levulinc acid and 2.5% SDS as a dip treatment is as efficacious as a double hurdle approach in reducing L. monocytogens on cantaloupes.
single hurdle application of 5% LA and 2% SDS in the packing plant is effective at reducing L. monocytogens at the stem scar of cantaloup.

application of 5% LA and 2% SDS at the packing plant as a single hurdle or in the field and the packing plant as double hurdles significantly reduced the L. monocytogens population compared to a simulated dip treatment with 200 ppm chlorine at the packing plant.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of sanitizers in the packing shed can reduce L. monocytogens on cantaloupes but that the use of multiple treatments in combination with a sanitizer in the packing shed is not necessarily beneficial.

the application of sanitizers at the packing plant can reduce the L. monocytegenes population on cantaloupes, but that the greatest reductions can be obtained by applying sanitizers in both the field and at packing plant operations.

a double hurdle approach to sanitizer applications in packing sheds is not as effective in reducing L. monocytogens populations as a single hurdle approach, or as application of sanitizers at the packing plant and in the field.
